correctness.rationale: The source generic tree can be recovered as an infinitely branching macro-tree whose incident macro-edges have lengths two and three, with infinitely many of each length at every branch vertex. Automorphisms preserve branch vertices and macro-edge length. Conversely, finite rooted color-preserving macro-tree isomorphisms extend by back-and-forth because each vertex has infinitely many unused incident edges of each color. Hence a point in a sphere about a branch vertex is classified by the sequence of completed macro-edge lengths together with its terminal position. If \(c_n\) counts compositions of \(n\) with parts two and three, then \(q_n=c_n+2c_{n-1}+c_{n-2}\), giving \((1+z)^2/(1-z^2-z^3)\), the recurrence \(q_n=q_{n-2}+q_{n-3}\), and the stated initial values. A fresh independent dynamic-programming reconstruction through radius thirty reproduced the profile and recurrence.

originality.rationale: The primary weak-amalgamation paper gives an explicit complete description of this generic limit: start with the unique countable everywhere-infinitely-branching tree, color incident edges in two infinite classes, and subdivide the two classes into paths of lengths two and three. Once that exact object is published, the audited radial orbit profile is a direct standard consequence: rooted automorphisms of the infinitely branching two-colored tree are transitive on paths with the same color word, and counting path lengths is exactly counting compositions with parts two and three. The Padovan recurrence and plastic-constant growth are therefore mechanically encoded in the source construction even though the source does not print those numbers.
